summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for evaluation of an upper gastrointestinal bleed after reporting blood-tinged emesis and a drop in hematocrit from 43.5 to 32.7. Given his history of Hep C cirrhosis and esophageal varices, he was monitored closely with serial hematocrits, which stabilized and improved to 34.9, suggesting no ongoing active bleeding. He was continued on IV pantoprazole and observed without need for transfusion. He had significant fluid retention due to noncompliance with diuretics, having gained 25 pounds recently; after receiving IV furosemide and restarting spironolactone, he had good urine output and symptom improvement. An abdominal ultrasound revealed cirrhosis and an 8-mm indeterminate liver lesion, prompting a recommendation for MRI follow-up. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout and was discharged home with medication adjustments and instructions to resume all prescribed therapies, including diuretics, and to follow up in the liver clinic.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission
